ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Three lines disect a big triangle into four triangles and three quadrilaterals. The sum of the perimeters of the three quadrialterals is $25 \mathrm{~cm}$. The sum of the perimeters of the four triangles is $20 \mathrm{~cm}$. The perimeter of the big triangle is $19 \mathrm{~cm}$. How big is the sum of the lengths of the three dissecting lines?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there is a large triangle, with three dissecting line segments drawn inside. These three internal line segments cross one another and connect to the sides or vertices of the large triangle, dividing the large triangle into seven small regions; the problem states that these small regions include four triangles and three quadrilaterals. Reasoning: The total perimeter of the four small triangles is 20 cm, and the total perimeter of the three small quadrilaterals is 25 cm, so the total perimeter of all the small regions is 20 + 25 = 45 cm. When adding the perimeters of all the small regions, the outer boundary of the large triangle is counted only once, namely 19 cm; each internal dissecting line is counted twice because it is a common side of two adjacent small regions. Let the total length of the three dissecting lines be L, then 45 = 19 + 2L. Solving gives 2L = 26, L = 13 cm.

The sum of the perimeters of the four triangles is $20\mathrm{~cm}$. The perimeter of the big triangle is $19\mathrm{~cm}$. What is the sum of the lengths of the three dissecting lines?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as one large triangle cut by three interior line segments into seven regions: four triangular regions and three quadrilateral regions. From the text, add the total perimeters of all small regions: 20 + 25 = 45 cm. In the sum of all small-region perimeters, the original outside boundary of the big triangle is counted once, while every interior dissecting segment is counted twice because it borders two adjacent regions. Let L be the total length of the three dissecting lines. Use 45 = 19 + 2L, so L = (45 - 19)/2 = 13 cm.
